questions: Cannot verify Qt leakage in core files - the diff does not show the includes section of core.cpp or profile_registry.cpp. The repo context claims these are 'Qt-free' but I need to see the full file to confirm no Qt headers are included.

After removing g_initialized atomic, is there any other global state in core.cpp that requires initialization ordering or thread-safe access? The code comment says core needs no init, but I need to verify no static initialization order fiasco is possible.
The bridge removal of m_initialized tracking - was this used anywhere else in the codebase besides the init/shutdown pair? Could there be dangling references to coreInitialized property?
nits: core.h comment could be more explicit about the 'always returns ECUIO_OK' contract - consider adding a note that callers should not attempt error handling for ecuio_init().
The bridge code change from 'm_initialized = (ecuio_init() == ECUIO_OK)' to '(void)ecuio_init()' is correct but could use a more explicit comment explaining why the result is discarded.
Consider adding a unit test that verifies ecuio_init() and ecuio_shutdown() can be called in any order, any number of times, and ecuio_session_create still works without ever calling init.
